question: What does the existing inscription pipeline actually produce when fed the wenyan.corpus.v1 classical corpus, and how much of that output discriminates between passages?
corpus: data/corpus — wenyan.corpus.v1, 16 works, 877 sections, 8208 passages, 906907 characters
baseline: mountain/wenyan@6143e22ca8319a8ebca89b59a29f20158812b63f (the inscription modules as shipped in this bundle)
scope: Full census over every corpus passage through the legacy path (no relationModel), default profile preset, steps=3. Plus: opt-in relation-grammar coverage, and the acknowledgement gate behaviour.
protected: the corpus is read-only in this experiment
the acknowledgement gate keeps its documented meaning
no confidence band, score or generated sentence is treated as a philological result
success: Every passage is processed without error; the full output distribution is recorded, including any property that shows the output does not discriminate between inputs.
nonclaims: no philological or historical interpretation of any passage
no claim that the pipeline understands 諸子 or 儒家 text
no claim that the inscription pipeline was designed for, or is suited to, this genre
no natural-language understanding and no semantic admission
convergence scores are internal to this experimental objective, not accuracy or quality measures
this is not an evaluation of Wikisource transcription quality
